app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

args.diagnosis: Frontend is correctly configured to call the cart service at cart:8080 (matching the cart Service/Pod), but the frontend does not expose any client timeout or retry configuration for cart calls (no env vars or container args present). The cart depends on Valkey/Redis (VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379) and has an init container that blocks until Valkey is reachable, indicating cart can be blocked by Valkey. Combined, this indicates the frontend is likely using default/long HTTP client timeouts/retries and is not handling cart errors/timeouts explicitly, which will amplify latency when the cart is blocked on Redis (propagating/blocking requests).
args.reasoning: Findings: (1) frontend Deployment/Pod show CART_ADDR=cart:8080 (frontend env) and no environment variables or container args indicating client timeouts or retry behavior (kubectl describe deployment/frontend and pod). (2) cart Service exposes port 8080 with endpoints pointing to the cart pod (kubectl describe service/cart), and cart Deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and includes an init container that waits for valkey-cart:6379 (kubectl describe deployment/cart and replicaset). These unique data points show port/URL match but no frontend-configured timeouts/retries and a cart dependency that can block — supporting the hypothesis that frontend defaults amplify latency when cart is blocked on Redis.

final_report.root_cause: The cart service repeatedly failed to connect to its Valkey (Redis) backend at runtime (valkey-cart:6379). These connection failures produced System.ApplicationException 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' in the cart code, which were translated to gRPC FailedPrecondition responses and propagated upstream. The unavailable/unresponsive Valkey backend (valkey-cart) is the proximate cause; lack of client-side fail-fast timeouts in frontend amplified the impact into very large end-to-end latencies at frontend and frontend-proxy.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Cart pod logs contain repeated stack traces and error messages: System.ApplicationException 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore (EnsureRedisConnected() and EmptyCartAsync), present multiple times in recent logs. 2) Traces from frontend-proxy and frontend show very high latencies and include cart call sequences that surface these FailedPrecondition errors (e.g., traces 94bb26..., 0cbb83...). 3) Cart pod env var VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 matches the observed failing endpoint in stack traces. 4) Cart init container completed (it waits for valkey-cart:6379), and the valkey-cart Service has an endpoint (10.244.1.11:6379), so the problem appears at runtime (intermittent/unavailable Valkey process or proxying), not a static service name/port mismatch. 5) Frontend has no explicit client timeouts/retries configured and likely uses long/default timeouts, which allowed cart-induced delays to propagate and amplify into large top-level latencies.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 epicenter check (cart pod) — completed: confirmed cart-5df68c7b56-4wlj9 emits repeated Redis connection failures and the exact endpoint used (VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379). Priority-2 (cart <-> valkey-cart service) — completed: verified valkey-cart Service exists, exposes port 6379, and reports an endpoint backing it (10.244.1.11:6379). Priority-3 (frontend <-> cart) — completed: verified frontend calls cart:8080 and lacks explicit client timeouts/retries; this explains amplification of latency. Methods: kubectl describe of deployments/services/pods and inspection of cart application logs and distributed traces. Conclusion: runtime unavailability/unresponsiveness of the Valkey (valkey-cart) backend caused the cart failures; those failures cascaded to frontend and frontend-proxy, producing high latencies and error responses.
